units.translation: The letters di are contracted into ζ in the forms of the words ζαπρέπων and κάρζα for διαπρέπων and καρδία, which see.

Etym. Gud. p. 227, 40. Etym. MS. Paris. ap. Larcherum in Actis Academiae Inscr. Parisinae vol. 47 (or in Sturz's Appendix to Orion p. 213) and Gaisford p. 1161, and the grammarian codex Oxon. in Cramer's Anecd. Oxon. vol. 2 p. 443. Ζαγρεὺς, ὁ μεγάλως ἀγρεύων, as (ὦ Oxon.) πότνια γῆ Ζαγρεῦ τε θεῶν πανυπέρτατε πάντων, said the author of the Alcmaeonis (πάντων – ἔφη omitted by Oxon.). But some say that Zagreus is the son of Hades, as Aeschylus in Sisyphus (ἐν Σκύφῳ omitted by Oxon.) Ζαγρεῖ τε νῦν με (μοι Oxon.) καὶ πολυξένῳ χαίρειν. In Aegyptii (sic Cramerus after Larcherus. αἰγυπτί Oxon. αἰγύπτῳ Gud. and Paris.) he thus calls him (οὕτως α. δ. omitted by Oxon.) Pluto, the hunter, the most hospitable to the dead. Which Hermann corrected thus: Ζ. ὁ. μ. ἀ. “πότνια Γἢ – πάντων,” as the author of the Alcmaeonis said; as Aeschylus in Sisyphus (fr. 229) “Ζαγρεῖ τε νῦν με καὶ πολυξένῳ πατρὶ χαίρειν.” In Aegyptii he thus calls him Pluto. Then follows another excerpt: in Supplices (147) he calls Zeus, “τὸν γάϊον, | τὸν πολυξενώτατον | Ζῆνα τῶν κεκμηκότων.
ἥπερ ἐν δόμοισι βακχείας καλῆς ἰατρὸς ἐλπὶς ἦν, where Bamberger reads βακχείας ζάλης.
with hot missiles of the unapproachable fire-breathing storm
with a hurricane of wind and a storm of rain and thunder
so as not to have the surge of the wave in harbor
a fiery red, very thick, shaggy beard
and fiery curls of lightning flash forth

Thus Bamberger corrected what is in M: καὶ τὰ χρέα ἔπη, changed by Turnebus to τὰ χρεῖ᾽ ἔπη. In a different sense Theocritus 25, 6 said ὁδοῦ ζαχρεῖον ὁδίτην, meaning 'needing the road': which is the usual meaning of the adjective χρεῖος, as Aeschylus himself a little later at v. 202 said χρεῖος εἶ ξένη φυγάς. Different is the Homeric ζαχρηής, written by some as ζαχρειής and explained variously by others, on which see Thes. vol. 4 p. 10.
with words of reverence, lamentation, and great need, answer the strangers
Aeschylus used only a few forms of this verb. Present ζῶ ζῇς ζῶμεν ζῶσι, infinitive ζῆν, participle ζῶν ζῶσα, imperfect ἔζων third person ἔζη. vivo.
καὶ ζῶντα καὶ βλέποντα, where now χλωρόν τε καὶ β. from the gloss of Hesychius, about which see under χλωρός.
but an unexpected sudden death deprived him of life
what gain is it for me to live?
willing to share evils with the unwilling, my soul, living with the dead, with a kindred mind
but the living must suffer from adverse fortune
